newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castorseed down on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Indian castorseed down on speculative selling.

text.p: Indian castorseed June delivery dropped to 1,112/1,113 rupees per quintal on Tuesday from 1,118 rupees on speculative selling, traders said.
"Continued pressure from arrivals at the producing centres and sluggish overseas enquiries prompted fresh speculative selling," one trader said.
Daily average arrivals of castorseed in eastern India's Gujarat region remained higher at 40,000/45,000 bags (75 kg each), traders said.
"Foreign buyers are asking for Indian castor oil at 690 dollars per tonne while Indian offers are in the 705/710 dollar range," another trader said.

"The Forward Market Commission has granted permission for trading in castorseed September 1997 delivery and trading in the new contract will commence from Wednesday," said Dilip Thakkar, director of Bombay Oil Exchange.
"Castorseed September delivery is likely to open at a premium of 60/70 rupees per quintal compared to June delivery," he said.
Groundnut oil slid to 361/362 rupees per 10 kg from 364/365 on summer crop arrivals and as buyers kept to the sidelines on expectation of further price erosion in the coming days, traders said.
Imported palm-oil also dropped 2/3 rupees to 290 rupees per 10 kg on arrivals of about 5,000/6,000 tonnes at the Bombay port.
In Rajkot, spot groundnut oil was steady at 560 rupees per 15 kg.
